title: Foreign Exchange (Forex) Products and Risk Management
subtitle: Analyse a corporate client's FX exposure, price a birr forward, propose a hedge and control the bank's own risks
summary: Advise Ethiopian importers, exporters and investors on FX risk under the post-2024 regime, from exposure mapping and forward pricing to a full hedging proposal for a pharmaceutical importer.
audience: FX sales and treasury sales staff, corporate relationship managers and risk staff in Ethiopian banks with some FX experience, or who have completed the Level 1 FX course. Completing the trade finance and international banking course (1.c) is recommended.
objectives: Analyse a corporate customer's FX exposure and propose a hedging strategy
Price forwards and explain swaps and options conceptually, within what Ethiopian rules allow
Manage the credit, market and conduct risks of FX products for the bank
Explain rate expectations to clients using NBE, IMF and market data

runningCase.name: Gefersa Pharma Import PLC
runningCase.text: Gefersa Pharma Import PLC, a fictional Addis Ababa importer of medicines and medical supplies, has USD 5 million of 180-day supplier credit from an Indian manufacturer and asks Bank A for advice. It holds USD 400,000 in an FCY account, sells about 40% of its goods to public hospitals under 12-month fixed birr tenders and 60% to private pharmacies, and earned a net profit of Birr 96 million last year. Its finance manager, Hirut Alemayehu, works with Bank A's FX sales officer, Mekdes Haile. Across the course, learners map its exposure, price a forward from an illustrative spot mid of Birr 150.00, design a hedging policy, check the bank's limits and present a hedging proposal.

modules.title: Mapping a client's FX exposure
modules.summary: Find, measure and explain the foreign exchange risk inside a corporate customer's cash flows and balance sheet under Ethiopia's market-based regime.
objectives: Explain the post-2024 FX rules that shape what customers can and cannot do
Separate transaction, translation and economic exposure in a corporate client
Build a currency cash flow map and compute net exposure by period
Measure the effect of the 2024 depreciation on FX debt held on a balance sheet
Quantify the running case exposure under several rate outcomes

lessons.title: The FX regime your clients now live in
body: Since 29 July 2024, banks in Ethiopia buy and sell foreign currency at rates they negotiate freely with customers and with each other in an interbank market. The NBE publishes an indicative daily rate, but it is a reference, not a rate banks must use. For corporate customers this ended the long queue for allocated FX and replaced it with a price that moves every day.

The rules have kept moving. Goods exporters convert part of their proceeds and keep the rest in a retention account; the surrender share on goods exports was cut from 50% to 30% at MPC meeting No. 7 in July 2026. FXD/04/2026 let service exporters keep 100% of proceeds and allowed banks to offer forward rates, which is the starting point for this course.

items.label: July 2024
items.text: FXD/01/2024: freely negotiated rates, interbank market, indicative rate, 50% conversion and 50% retention for exporters

items.label: November 2025
items.text: SBB/96/2025: a bank's overall open FX position capped at plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 capital

items.label: February 2026
items.text: FXD/04/2026: forward rates allowed, 100% retention for service exporters, bank-level approval of remittances and external loans

items.label: May 2026
items.text: FXD/05/2026: banks approve LC and CAD on acceptance for FX account holders; FVD/01/2026 sets franco valuta import rules

items.label: July 2026
items.text: MPC No. 7: surrender on goods exports cut from 50% to 30%; NBE FX commission cut from 2.5% to 1.5%

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/01/2024, Foreign Exchange (in force 29 July 2024)
regulation.text: Banks may buy and sell foreign currency at freely negotiated rates and trade with each other in an interbank market; the NBE indicative rate is non-binding. Exporters must repatriate proceeds within three months (90 days), convert 50% to birr and may keep 50% in a retention account. The directive also sets import payment modes, the rules for foreign currency accounts and the rules for external loans. MPC No. 7 (July 2026) cut the goods-export surrender share to 30%; check the implementing directive before quoting it to a client.

lessons.tip: Rules changed five times in two years. Before any client meeting, check the latest NBE directive list and MPC release.

lessons.title: Transaction, translation and economic exposure
body: Transaction exposure is a known foreign currency amount to be paid or received on a known date: a supplier invoice in USD due in 180 days, or an export receivable in EUR due in 60 days. It is the easiest to measure and the one forwards are designed for.

Translation exposure arises when foreign currency assets or liabilities are restated in birr at each reporting date. Economic exposure is the slower, wider effect of the rate on a business model: a depreciation raises an importer's costs, but whether it hurts depends on whether the importer can raise birr prices before its competitors do.

items.label: Transaction
items.text: Known FCY amount, known date. Hedge with forwards or matching flows.

items.label: Translation
items.text: FCY assets and debts restated in birr each reporting date. Hits equity and covenants.

items.label: Economic
items.text: Effect on prices, demand and competitiveness over years. Managed through strategy.

example.title: Two clients, one depreciation
example.text: Kombolcha Leather Works PLC exports finished leather and buys tanning chemicals in USD. When the birr weakened, its birr revenue rose faster than its costs, and its margin widened. Hawassa Office Supplies PLC imports printers and sells in birr on fixed-price government contracts. The same move cut its margin by a third, because its contract prices could not change for twelve months. Same rate move, opposite outcomes: exposure is about the client's whole business, not just its invoices.

lessons.title: Building a currency cash flow map
body: Start with the client's own records: supplier contracts and credit terms, open LCs and CADs, export orders, FCY account and retention balances, external loans and their repayment schedules. Place every flow in a table by currency and by month or quarter for the next 12 months.

Net the inflows and outflows in each currency per period. The net figure, not the gross import bill, is the exposure the client needs to manage. Mark each line as committed (signed, dated) or forecast (expected but not contracted), because a bank hedges committed flows more confidently than forecasts.

items.label: Collect
items.text: Contracts, LCs, supplier credit terms, loan schedules, FCY balances

items.label: Place
items.text: Each flow by currency and month for 12 months

items.label: Tag
items.text: Committed or forecast

items.label: Net
items.text: Inflows minus outflows per currency per period

items.label: Stress
items.text: Birr value of the net position at several rates

worked.title: Gefersa Pharma Import: 12-month USD map (USD thousands)

rows.label: Months 3 to 12: new orders on CAD (forecast)
USD held in FCY account (from a shareholder loan)
Net committed exposure, month 6
rows.value: minus 4,600 after using the FCY balance

worked.note: The 180-day supplier credit is the committed exposure to hedge first. The forecast orders are real but uncertain, and deserve a lower hedge ratio.

scenario.title: Gross or net?
scenario.situation: Gefersa's finance manager, Hirut Alemayehu, tells the bank she needs to cover USD 5 million in six months. She also holds USD 400,000 in an FCY account that she plans to use for the same supplier.
scenario.question: What amount should the FX sales officer treat as the committed exposure for the month 6 payment?
scenario.explain: Exposure is the net figure. The FCY balance already offsets USD 400,000 of the payment, so only USD 4.6 million needs to be bought or hedged. Hedging the gross amount would over-hedge.

lessons.title: Natural hedges before financial hedges
body: A natural hedge is an offset inside the business. An exporter that also imports can pay suppliers from its retention account. A company can invoice some sales in USD where the rules allow, or put price adjustment clauses into birr contracts that link prices to the exchange rate.

Natural hedges are cheap but rarely perfect: timing and amounts seldom match. They also have to respect the rules, for example the 90-day repatriation requirement for export proceeds, which limits how long an exporter can delay bringing money home to match its payments.
points: Use retention and FCY account balances against FCY payments in the same period
Add exchange rate adjustment clauses to longer birr sales contracts
Shorten the gap between buying FX and pricing the goods
Borrow in birr, not USD, when revenue is in birr

example.title: A coffee exporter's built-in hedge
example.text: Yirgalem Coffee Export PLC sells about USD 6 million of coffee a year and imports USD 1.2 million of jute bags, hulling spares and a vehicle fleet. Its finance head, Abebe Gudeta, pays all USD costs from the retention account. Only the remaining surplus is converted to birr, so the business has no USD payables to hedge, only the question of when to convert its surplus.

scenario.title: Delaying conversion
scenario.situation: Yirgalem Coffee expects the birr to weaken and asks whether it can leave an export receipt abroad for five months before bringing it home, so it converts at a better rate.
scenario.question: What should the relationship manager say?
options: Yes, timing conversion is a normal natural hedge
Yes, if the client signs a forward contract
Only with written approval from the branch manager
No: proceeds must be repatriated within 90 days, and the surrender share must be converted; only the retained share can be held in FCY
scenario.explain: FXD/01/2024 requires repatriation within 90 days and conversion of the surrender share. The client can hold the retained share in its retention account, but cannot keep proceeds abroad to speculate on the rate.

lessons.title: FX debt on balance sheets after the 2024 depreciation
body: Many Ethiopian companies carried USD supplier credits, shareholder loans or external loans when the birr floated. Each reporting date, those liabilities are restated at the current rate. A large depreciation inflates the birr value of the debt and books a loss through profit or loss, even though not one more dollar is owed.

For the bank, this matters in three ways. Equity falls, so leverage covenants can break. Debt service in birr rises, so DSCR falls. And collateral values do not rise at the same pace, so loan-to-value ratios on birr collateral securing FX-linked exposure can weaken.

worked.title: Translation of a USD 2 million supplier credit (illustrative rates)

rows.label: Birr value when booked at Birr 57.00
Birr value at a later reporting rate of Birr 120.00

worked.note: Equity fell by 42% from translation alone. A debt to equity covenant set before the float may now be breached even though trading is sound.

scenario.title: A covenant breach from translation
scenario.situation: Sululta Ceramics PLC reports that its debt to equity ratio rose from 1.5 to 2.6, above its 2.0 covenant. The cause is an unrealised loss on a USD 3 million shareholder loan. Sales and cash flow are steady.
scenario.question: What is the most sensible first response from the relationship manager?
options: Call the loan immediately for covenant breach
Ignore the breach because the loss is unrealised
Ask the client to restate the loan at the old rate
Analyse cash flow and the loan's real repayment terms, then consider a waiver with a plan to hedge or convert the FX debt
scenario.explain: The breach is real and must be handled, but cash flow is the first way out. A waiver with conditions, such as a hedge or a conversion of the shareholder loan to equity, protects the bank better than an immediate call. Restating at an old rate would break accounting rules.

lessons.title: The running case: Gefersa's exposure in birr
body: Gefersa Pharma Import PLC owes its Indian supplier USD 5 million in 180 days. At the illustrative mid rate of Birr 150.00 the debt is worth Birr 750 million today. Hirut wants to know what happens if the birr moves, and whether she can still sell at today's prices.

About 40% of Gefersa's sales are to public hospitals under 12-month fixed birr tenders; the other 60% go to private pharmacies, which can absorb price rises with a lag. So part of the exposure can be passed on, and part cannot. This mix, not just the USD amount, drives the hedging proposal in Module 4.

worked.title: Gefersa: birr cost of USD 5 million in 180 days

rows.label: If the rate reaches Birr 165.00 (10% weaker)
If the rate reaches Birr 180.00 (20% weaker)
Gefersa's annual net profit (FY last year)
Extra cost at Birr 180.00 as a share of a year's profit

worked.note: A 20% move would wipe out more than a full year's profit. The exposure is material and should be managed, not ignored.

visual.caption: Birr cost of the USD 5 million supplier credit at three rates (course worked example).

takeaways: Since July 2024, FX is priced by the market; the NBE indicative rate is a reference only.
Separate transaction, translation and economic exposure; forwards address the first.
Measure net exposure by currency and period, and tag committed versus forecast flows.
Use natural hedges first, within the repatriation and conversion rules.
Translation losses on FX debt can break covenants and weaken DSCR without any change in trading.

quiz.q: Under FXD/01/2024, the NBE indicative daily rate is:
options: The rate every bank must use
The rate for government imports only
quiz.explain: Banks negotiate rates freely; the indicative rate is a reference.

quiz.q: A USD invoice of known amount due on a known date is an example of:
quiz.explain: Known amount and date make it a transaction exposure.

quiz.q: A client owes USD 3.0 million in 90 days and holds USD 0.8 million in its FCY account for the same payment. Net committed exposure is:
quiz.explain: 3.0 minus 0.8 = USD 2.2 million.

quiz.q: Within how many days must exporters repatriate proceeds under FXD/01/2024?
quiz.explain: The directive sets a three-month (90-day) repatriation period.

quiz.q: A USD 1 million loan booked at Birr 60 is restated at Birr 130. The unrealised loss is:
quiz.explain: 1 million x (130 minus 60) = Birr 70 million.

quiz.q: Which client is most exposed to economic exposure from a weaker birr?
options: A service exporter that keeps 100% retention
An importer selling on fixed birr prices for 12 months
A company with no FX flows and only local competitors
quiz.explain: Its costs rise while its selling prices are fixed.

modules.title: Forwards: pricing, documentation and settlement
modules.summary: Price a birr forward from interest rate parity, turn it into a client rate, and document and settle it correctly.
objectives: Explain what a forward contract is and what FXD/04/2026 allows
Derive a forward rate from interest rate parity and compute forward points
Build a client forward price from mid rate, spread and credit charge
Describe the documents, settlement steps and what happens when dates change

lessons.title: What a forward is, and why it is new in Ethiopia
body: A forward is a binding agreement to exchange a fixed amount of one currency for another at a rate fixed today, on a date in the future. The client knows its birr cost now; the bank takes on the obligation to deliver at that rate.

Before 2026 Ethiopian banks did not offer forward rates to customers. FXD/04/2026 changed this. For an importer like Gefersa, a forward turns an unknown birr cost into a known one, which makes pricing tenders and planning cash much easier.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/04/2026, Amendment to Foreign Exchange Directive No. FXD/01/2024 (in force 12 February 2026)
regulation.text: The amendment allows banks to offer forward rates to customers. It also lets service exporters keep 100% of proceeds in retention accounts, and lets banks approve dividend and profit remittances, external loans and supplier credits without prior NBE approval, with monthly reporting to the NBE. Each bank's own product rules, limits and documentation still apply.

left.title: Spot
items: Delivery now (within the bank's settlement time)
Client bears all future rate risk

right.title: Forward
items: Delivery on an agreed future date
Client's birr cost is locked; bank carries counterparty and position risk

lessons.title: Interest rate parity: where the forward rate comes from
body: A forward rate is not the bank's forecast. It is the rate at which the bank can lock in delivery without taking a view. To sell USD forward, the bank can borrow birr, buy USD spot and invest the USD until the delivery date. Its cost is the birr interest paid minus the USD interest earned.

So the forward rate equals spot multiplied by the ratio of the two interest factors. When birr rates are much higher than USD rates, as in Ethiopia, the forward rate for buying USD is well above spot. Think of the gap as the price of carry, not a prediction.

visual.caption: Day count conventions differ by market; this course uses days/360 for both legs for teaching.

example.title: Why the forward is above spot
example.text: Mekdes Haile, an FX sales officer at Bank A, explains it to a client this way: if I sell you dollars in six months, I must buy them today and hold them. To buy them I give up birr that could earn around 15% a year in the money market, and I earn only about 4% a year on the dollars. You pay me the difference in the forward rate. If birr and dollar rates were equal, the forward would equal spot.

lessons.title: Forward points with high birr rates
body: Forward points are the forward rate minus spot. In birr markets they are large and positive for USD purchases because the interest gap is wide. Points grow with tenor: roughly double for 180 days compared with 90 days.

The course example uses an illustrative birr money market rate of 15% (close to the 7-day interbank rate of 14.6% and the National Bank Rate of 16% reported at MPC No. 7) and an illustrative USD rate of 4%. Your treasury will give you the live inputs; the method stays the same.

worked.title: Forward points, USD/ETB (illustrative inputs)

rows.label: Annualised forward premium, 180 days: (158.09 / 150.00 minus 1) x 2

worked.note: The 180-day forward premium of about 10.8% a year mirrors the 11-point interest gap. It is the cost of carry, not a forecast.

scenario.title: Is the forward a forecast?
scenario.situation: Hirut at Gefersa sees the 180-day forward mid of 158.09 and says: 'So your bank expects the birr to weaken to 158 in six months.'
scenario.question: What is the correct reply?
options: Yes, forward rates are the bank's forecast
No, the forward is set by the NBE
No, the forward reflects the interest rate gap between birr and USD; the future spot rate could be above or below it
scenario.explain: Forwards come from interest rate parity. They are the no-view price of delivering later, and the actual future spot rate may be higher or lower.

lessons.title: From mid rate to client price
body: The forward mid is the starting point. To get the client rate, the bank adds its sales spread (the same idea as the spot buy and sell spread) and a charge for the credit and liquidity risk it takes over the life of the contract. Longer tenors and weaker counterparties carry higher charges.

Show the client the build-up. Transparent pricing helps the client compare banks and protects your bank from later complaints. Compare the forward cost with the risk it removes, not just with today's spot rate.

worked.title: Gefersa: 180-day forward to buy USD 5 million (illustrative)

rows.label: Compared with buying at today's spot ask of 151.20
Compared with an unhedged outcome at Birr 180.00 ask

worked.note: The forward costs about 5.5% over today's spot ask but removes the risk of a much larger loss. It also gives Gefersa a known cost for its tender pricing.

scenario.title: Pricing for a weaker client
scenario.situation: Two importers each ask for a 180-day forward on USD 1 million. Gefersa has a strong credit grade and a secured credit line. Debre Zeit Auto Parts PLC has a weaker grade, declining sales and no line yet.
scenario.question: How should the bank price and approve them?
options: Same rate for both, because the market rate is the same
Lower charge for Debre Zeit to win the business
Higher credit charge for Debre Zeit and approval of a counterparty limit before dealing, possibly with a margin deposit
scenario.explain: The market part of the price is the same; the credit charge is not. A weaker client needs a counterparty limit first and a higher charge or a cash margin.

lessons.title: Documentation and settlement
body: A forward needs a signed framework agreement with the client (general terms, events of default, close-out), a deal confirmation for each trade (amount, rate, value date, settlement accounts) and evidence of the underlying transaction where the bank's product rules require it, such as the supplier credit agreement, proforma invoice or import permit.

On the value date, the client pays birr and the bank pays USD to the supplier or credits the client's FCY account. Settlement instructions should be agreed at the trade date to avoid errors. Every deal is booked the same day so treasury sees its position and credit sees the limit use.

items.label: Limit
items.text: Counterparty limit approved by credit

items.label: Agreement
items.text: Framework agreement signed once

items.label: Quote and deal
items.text: Rate agreed, recorded call or written request

items.label: Confirm
items.text: Confirmation sent and signed the same day

items.label: Monitor
items.text: Track mark-to-market and limit use

items.label: Settle
items.text: Birr in, USD out on the value date

lessons.tip: Never deal before the limit and the framework agreement are in place. A forward without documents is an unsecured promise.

lessons.title: When the date or the amount changes
body: Shipments slip and supplier terms change. If the client needs the USD earlier, the bank can deliver early and adjust the rate for the shorter period. If the client needs it later, the contract can be extended by closing it and opening a new one, with the gain or loss on the old contract settled or rolled at the bank's discretion.

If the underlying deal is cancelled, the client still owes the bank the result of closing the contract at the current market rate. This is a key point to explain before the first deal, because clients often think a forward can simply be walked away from.

example.title: A delayed shipment
example.text: Bahir Dar Agro Inputs PLC bought USD 800,000 forward for 90 days at 154.80 to pay for fertiliser blending equipment. The supplier delayed shipment by 60 days. Bank A closed the original contract and booked a new 60-day forward. Because the birr had weakened, the close-out left a small gain, which the client chose to apply to the new rate. The finance manager, Getachew Worku, said the conversation was easy only because the bank had explained extensions before the first trade.

scenario.title: A cancelled order
scenario.situation: Gefersa's supplier cancels part of an order, so Gefersa needs only USD 4 million instead of USD 5 million in 180 days. It asks to cancel USD 1 million of the forward. Since the deal, the forward rate for that date has fallen from 158.09 to 155.00.
scenario.question: What is the right outcome?
options: The USD 1 million is closed out at the current rate and Gefersa pays the loss of about Birr 3.09 per USD, roughly Birr 3.1 million
The bank cancels USD 1 million at no cost
The bank must deliver all USD 5 million
scenario.explain: A forward is binding. Closing part of it at the current market rate crystallises a loss of (158.09 minus 155.00) x 1 million, which the client pays, as the framework agreement should state.

takeaways: FXD/04/2026 allows banks to offer forward rates; each bank's product rules, limits and documents still apply.
Forward rate = spot x birr interest factor / USD interest factor; it is the cost of carry, not a forecast.
With birr rates far above USD rates, forward points are large and grow with tenor.
Client price = forward mid + sales spread + credit and liquidity charge, shown transparently.
Forwards are binding: explain early delivery, extension and close-out before the first deal.

quiz.q: Spot 150.00, birr rate 12%, USD rate 4%, 90 days (days/360). The forward mid is closest to:
Why is the USD/ETB forward rate above spot?
options: Birr interest rates are higher than USD rates
quiz.explain: Interest rate parity: higher birr rates push the forward above spot.

quiz.q: Forward mid 158.09, spread 1.20, credit charge 0.40. Client forward rate?
Which document records each individual forward trade?
quiz.explain: Each trade gets its own confirmation with amount, rate and value date.

quiz.q: A client's underlying import is cancelled. The forward contract:
options: Must still be settled or closed out at market
quiz.explain: A forward is binding; close-out at market settles it.

quiz.q: If birr and USD interest rates were equal, the forward rate would be:
quiz.explain: With equal interest factors the ratio is 1, so forward equals spot.

modules.title: Swaps and options: concepts and what Ethiopian rules allow
modules.summary: Understand FX swaps, cross-currency swaps and vanilla options, and tell clients clearly which tools are available onshore today.
objectives: Explain how an FX swap and a cross-currency swap work and who uses them
Read the payoff of a vanilla call or put option and its premium cost
Distinguish what the directives received allow from what is not yet available
Discuss offshore hedging for project loans within the external loan rules

lessons.title: FX swaps: a spot and a forward in one deal
body: An FX swap combines two trades with the same counterparty: exchange currencies today at spot and reverse the exchange on a future date at the forward rate. Neither party takes an open position; the swap moves liquidity from one currency to another for a period.

Banks use swaps to fund FX or birr temporarily. A corporate with spare USD now and a USD payment in three months can swap the USD into birr, earn birr interest, and get the USD back on the payment date. The price of the swap is the forward points, which are set by the interest gap.

items.label: Today
items.text: Client gives USD 1 million, receives birr at spot 150.00

items.label: Meanwhile
items.text: Client uses or invests the birr

items.label: In 90 days
items.text: Client returns birr at forward 154.08, receives USD 1 million back

example.title: Idle dollars, a birr cash need
example.text: Mekelle Textile Mills PLC holds USD 1 million in its retention account for machinery due in 90 days, but faces a short birr payroll and tax gap. A swap would let it use birr for 90 days and still have USD for the supplier. Bank A's treasury explained the idea to its CFO, Tsion Gebre, but noted that the bank would first confirm with compliance that a customer swap of retention balances is consistent with current rules, since the directives summarised for this course do not address customer swaps directly.

lessons.title: Cross-currency swaps for long-term debt
body: A cross-currency swap is a longer-term contract in which two parties exchange principal in two currencies and then exchange interest payments over several years, swapping principal back at the end. It can turn a USD loan into a synthetic birr loan for a borrower whose revenues are in birr.

Pricing a long-dated USD/ETB swap needs a deep birr yield curve and long-term counterparties willing to take birr risk. Those conditions are only starting to develop in Ethiopia, so such swaps are rare and usually arranged offshore with development lenders that have a specific mandate.

left.title: FX swap
items: Short term, often under one year

right.title: Cross-currency swap
items: Long term, often matches a loan
Needs long-term yield curves in both currencies
Used to change the currency of debt

lessons.title: Vanilla options: the right, not the obligation
body: A USD call option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy USD at a fixed strike rate on a future date. The buyer pays a premium up front. If the market rate ends above the strike, the buyer exercises; if below, the buyer lets the option lapse and buys at the better market rate.

Options give protection with upside, at a cost. The premium depends on the strike, tenor, interest rates and above all volatility. In a market that has just moved from a managed rate to a float, volatility is high and hard to estimate, so premiums would be expensive and hard to price reliably.

worked.title: USD call option, strike 160.00, premium Birr 4.00 per USD (illustrative)

rows.label: Rate at expiry 150.00: lapse, buy at market
Rate at expiry 180.00: exercise at strike

worked.note: The option caps the cost at 164.00 and keeps the benefit if the birr strengthens. The forward is cheaper in the bad case but gives up the upside.

scenario.title: Which tool fits?
scenario.situation: Gefersa expects to bid for a large public hospital tender in four months, but is not sure it will win. If it wins, it will need USD 2 million.
scenario.question: Which hedge best fits a contingent exposure like this, in principle?
options: An option, because the exposure may not happen
No hedge is ever needed for a tender
scenario.explain: An option protects without obliging the client to buy USD it may not need. A forward on an exposure that may vanish could leave Gefersa with a close-out loss. Whether an option is available onshore is a separate question covered next.

lessons.title: What is and is not yet permitted
body: The NBE Proclamation requires FX business to go through banks and authorised dealers. The directives received for this course explicitly allow banks to offer forward rates to customers (FXD/04/2026). They do not set rules for customer FX options or customer cross-currency swaps, so treat these as not yet available onshore until the NBE says otherwise.

The FX Market Operation Guideline and Code of Conduct referred to in FXD/01/2024 may add detail on interbank swaps and market conduct; it was not among the texts reviewed for this course. When a client asks for any product beyond spot and forwards, check with treasury and compliance before saying yes or no.

regulation.source: National Bank of Ethiopia Proclamation No. 1359/2025
regulation.text: Foreign exchange transactions are carried out only through banks and authorised dealers (Art. 39). Read together with FXD/01/2024 and its amendments, this means a customer FX product must be offered by a licensed bank within the rules the NBE has issued. FXD/04/2026 adds forward rates; products the directives do not mention need confirmation before they are offered.

left.title: Available under the directives reviewed
items: Spot purchase and sale at negotiated rates
LC and CAD on acceptance approved by banks for FX account holders (FXD/05/2026)

right.title: Not addressed: confirm before offering
items: Customer FX swaps of retention balances

scenario.title: An offshore option offer
scenario.situation: A foreign bank emails Hirut offering Gefersa a USD/ETB option settled offshore in USD. She asks Bank A's RM whether she should accept.
scenario.question: What should the RM advise?
options: Do not deal until compliance confirms the arrangement fits Ethiopian FX rules, since FX business must go through licensed banks and authorised dealers; meanwhile discuss a forward
Accept, it is a private matter between Gefersa and the foreign bank
Accept, as long as the premium is paid from the retention account
scenario.explain: Proclamation No. 1359/2025 (Art. 39) channels FX through banks and authorised dealers. An offshore contract by a resident company may conflict with that and with FXD/01/2024. The RM should not give a legal opinion but should flag the risk and offer the permitted tool.

lessons.title: Offshore hedging for project loans
body: Large projects often borrow in USD or EUR from development finance institutions or foreign lenders. Since FXD/04/2026, banks may approve external loans and supplier credits without prior NBE approval, with monthly reporting, while FXD/01/2024 rules such as the 60:40 debt to equity cap for foreign investors' external loans still apply.

If the project's revenue is in birr, the borrower carries a large currency mismatch for many years. Some lenders offer an embedded hedge or a local-currency loan priced off a currency risk fund. The Ethiopian bank's role is to help the client see the mismatch, include it in the cash flow model and check that any hedge fits the external loan approval.

example.title: A solar plant with a USD loan
example.text: Afar Sun Energy PLC, a fictional independent power producer, plans a USD 40 million loan from a development lender for a solar plant. Its tariff is paid in birr. A 20% depreciation would raise annual debt service in birr by the same proportion and push the DSCR below the lender's covenant. The sponsor is negotiating a tariff partly indexed to USD and a currency hedge provided by the lender's partner fund, both offshore. Bank A, as the account bank, reviews the external loan file and the hedge terms before approving the loan registration.

scenario.title: A mismatch in a project
scenario.situation: A hotel developer in Bishoftu asks Bank A to approve a USD 12 million external loan. Revenue will be about 70% in birr from local guests and 30% in USD from foreign guests. Debt service is 100% in USD.
scenario.question: What is the RM's key concern?
options: The currency mismatch: about 70% of revenue is in birr against all-USD debt service, so the model must stress the rate and the structure should reduce the mismatch
None: FXD/04/2026 lets banks approve external loans
scenario.explain: Approval authority moved to banks, which makes the bank responsible for judging the risk. A stressed DSCR at weaker birr rates is essential.

lessons.title: Doing more with the tools available
body: Even with a short product list, a good FX adviser has many levers. Forwards can be layered across dates. Retention and FCY balances can be matched to payments. Payment terms can be renegotiated with suppliers. LCs and CADs on acceptance, which banks can now approve for FX account holders under FXD/05/2026, can align payment timing with the client's FX inflows.
Pricing clauses in sales contracts move part of the risk to customers. Borrowing in birr for birr assets avoids building mismatches in the first place. Combine these before proposing anything exotic.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/05/2026, Amendment to Foreign Exchange Directive No. FXD/01/2024 (in force 25 May 2026)
regulation.text: Banks may approve letters of credit on acceptance and cash against documents on acceptance without prior NBE approval for institutions with foreign currency accounts, including retention account holders. These institutions may order shipments before bank approval, with payment processed after documents are submitted and verified. An accompanying NBE notice says LC fees are priced on an annualised basis, pro-rated to tenor.

points: Layer forwards across several value dates
Match FCY balances to payment dates
Negotiate supplier credit or acceptance terms
Add rate adjustment clauses to birr sales contracts

takeaways: An FX swap is a spot plus a reverse forward; its price is the forward points.
Cross-currency swaps change the currency of long-term debt but need deep yield curves.
Options protect with upside at the cost of a premium that is high when volatility is high.
The directives reviewed allow customer forwards; options and customer swaps are not addressed, so confirm before offering.
Under FXD/04/2026 banks approve external loans, so they must also judge the currency mismatch.

quiz.q: An FX swap consists of:
options: A spot trade and a reverse forward trade
A loan and a deposit in the same currency
quiz.explain: Exchange at spot, reverse at the forward rate.

quiz.q: A USD call with strike 160 and premium 4 is held when the rate ends at 170. Effective cost per USD?
quiz.explain: Exercise at 160 plus premium 4 = 164.

quiz.q: Same option, rate ends at 152. Effective cost per USD?
quiz.explain: Let it lapse, buy at 152, plus premium 4 = 156.

quiz.q: Which customer product is explicitly allowed by FXD/04/2026?
quiz.explain: The amendment allows banks to offer forward rates.

quiz.q: Under the NBE Proclamation, FX transactions are carried out through:
quiz.explain: Art. 39 channels FX through banks and authorised dealers.

quiz.q: A project with birr revenue and a USD loan has:
options: No FX risk because the loan is long term
A currency mismatch to stress in the cash flow model
quiz.explain: Birr revenue against USD debt service is a mismatch that hits DSCR when the birr weakens.

modules.title: Hedging strategy, policy and market outlook
modules.summary: Design a corporate hedging policy, choose hedge ratios that balance cost and protection, and explain rate expectations responsibly.
objectives: Set out the parts of a corporate FX hedging policy
Choose and justify a hedge ratio for committed and forecast exposures
Compare outcomes of different hedge ratios across rate scenarios
Give an overview of hedge accounting under IFRS 9
Use NBE, IMF and market data to explain rate expectations without making promises

lessons.title: Designing a hedging policy for a corporate
body: A hedging policy is a short board-approved document that stops FX decisions from being made by mood. It states why the company hedges, which exposures are covered, which instruments are allowed, how much is hedged and for how long, who may deal, and how results are reported.

The bank can help the client write it, but the decisions are the client's. A policy also protects the client's managers: if the birr strengthens after a hedge, the policy shows the hedge was a planned risk decision, not a bad bet.

items.label: Objective
items.text: Protect margins and cash, not profit from rates

items.label: Exposures
items.text: Which flows: committed, forecast, debt

items.label: Instruments
items.text: Spot, forwards and natural hedges; only what the rules permit

items.label: Ratios and tenors
items.text: How much and how far ahead

items.label: Authority
items.text: Who may deal and up to what amount

items.label: Reporting
items.text: Monthly report to management, quarterly to the board

example.title: A policy after a painful year
example.text: Dire Dawa Cement Distributors PLC lost Birr 40 million in 2025 on unhedged USD payables. Its board, led by chair Meseret Lemma, adopted a one-page policy: hedge 80% to 100% of committed payables within six months and 30% to 50% of forecast payables for months seven to twelve, using forwards only, with every deal above USD 500,000 approved by the CFO and reported monthly. The next year's results were far more predictable.

lessons.title: Hedge ratios and layering
body: The hedge ratio is the share of an exposure that is hedged. Committed exposures can be hedged at high ratios because they will happen. Forecast exposures deserve lower ratios because they may change. Many companies use a declining ladder: high ratios for near months, lower ones further out.

Layering means building hedges in steps over time rather than all on one day. It averages the rate and reduces the regret of choosing one day badly. For Gefersa, the part of the exposure that cannot be passed on to customers, the fixed-price tender sales, is the part most worth hedging.

worked.title: Gefersa: proposed hedge ratio for the USD 4.6 million committed exposure

rows.label: Share of sales on fixed 12-month birr tenders
Share of sales to private pharmacies (price pass-through with a lag)
Reason
rows.value: Covers all tender-linked cost plus part of the pass-through lag

worked.note: 70% protects the margin on fixed-price tenders with room to spare, and leaves some exposure open where prices can adjust.

scenario.title: Choosing the ratio
scenario.situation: Hirut wants to hedge 100% of the USD 4.6 million. Her CEO, Samuel Tadesse, wants 0% because he believes the birr will stabilise. About 40% of sales are fixed-price tenders.
scenario.question: Which recommendation is best supported by the analysis?
options: 100%, because any open exposure is speculation
About 70%, covering at least the fixed-price tender share with a margin for the pass-through lag, and documented in a policy
50% because it is a neutral number
scenario.explain: The ratio should follow the business: costs that cannot be passed on deserve protection. A documented ratio between the extremes avoids betting on a view either way.

lessons.title: Cost versus protection
body: Every hedge has a visible cost and an invisible benefit. Against today's spot, the forward looks expensive. Against a bad outcome, it looks cheap. The honest comparison shows the client what each choice produces across a range of future rates.

Use three or four scenarios, include one where the birr strengthens, and show the result for each hedge ratio. The client should choose the ratio whose worst case it can live with, not the one that would have been best in hindsight.

worked.title: Gefersa: birr cost of USD 4.6 million at three outcomes (forward 159.59, ask at outcome)
worked.note: At 70% the worst case is Birr 762 million instead of Birr 828 million, and the range of outcomes shrinks by 70%. The price is about Birr 31 million of lost upside if the birr stays at 150.

visual.caption: Worst-case birr cost of the committed exposure by hedge ratio (course worked example).

lessons.title: Hedge accounting in brief
body: Under IFRS, a forward is a derivative measured at fair value, with changes going through profit or loss. The hedged supplier invoice may be recognised later and on a different basis. Without hedge accounting, profit can swing even when the economic hedge works perfectly.

IFRS 9 allows hedge accounting when the company documents the hedge relationship at inception, shows an economic relationship between the hedge and the hedged item, and sets the hedge ratio. For a forecast purchase, a cash flow hedge holds the forward's gains and losses in equity until the purchase affects profit. Clients reporting under IFRS should involve their auditors early.
points: Document the risk management objective and the hedged item at the start
Show the economic relationship and the hedge ratio
Choose cash flow hedge for forecast purchases, fair value hedge for recognised items
Agree the approach with the auditor before the first deal

scenario.title: A profit swing
scenario.situation: Gefersa hedged a forecast purchase with a forward. At the half-year, the birr strengthened and the forward shows a Birr 12 million fair value loss in profit or loss, while the purchase is not yet recorded. The CEO says the hedge 'lost money'.
scenario.question: What would have avoided the profit swing?
options: Hiding the forward off balance sheet
Documenting the forward as a cash flow hedge under IFRS 9 at inception, so effective changes go to equity until the purchase affects profit
Asking the bank to delay booking the deal
scenario.explain: Hedge accounting aligns the timing of the forward's result with the hedged purchase. The economic hedge was sound; the accounting needed documentation from day one.

lessons.title: Reading NBE, IMF and market data
body: Clients will ask where the birr is going. Answer with sources, not opinions. The NBE MPC release gives the policy rate, inflation and interbank conditions. The indicative daily rate and the bank's own interbank trades show the recent trend. IMF programme review documents discuss reserves, the FX market and policy commitments.

One simple lens is the inflation gap. If Ethiopian inflation runs well above US inflation, the birr tends to weaken over time to keep prices comparable. It is a long-run tendency, not a forecast for a given month, and capital flows, aid and policy can dominate in the short run.

regulation.source: NBE Monetary Policy Committee meeting No. 7, press release (13 July 2026)
regulation.text: The NBE Board raised the National Bank Rate by 1 point to 16%, with the corridor of plus or minus 3 points unchanged, removed the credit growth cap, cut the NBE FX commission from 2.5% to 1.5% and cut the surrender requirement on goods exports from 50% to 30%. The release reported headline inflation of 13.4% in May 2026, a 91-day T-bill yield of 11.0% and a 7-day interbank rate of 14.6%. Update these figures from the latest release before using them with clients.

worked.title: The inflation gap as a rough guide (illustrative US inflation)

rows.label: Reading
rows.value: The forward premium is close to the inflation gap

worked.note: If the inflation gap persists, the forward is not an expensive bet against the market: it is close to what relative prices suggest. This is context for the client, not a forecast.

lessons.title: Explaining rate expectations to clients
body: An FX salesperson's view can sound like a promise. Present a range of outcomes, name the sources, explain the drivers on both sides (export earnings, remittances, aid and FDI against import demand and debt service) and remind the client that the hedge decision rests on its policy, not on the bank's view.
Record what you said. If the client later suffers a loss, a note showing balanced information protects the bank and shows fair treatment.

example.title: A balanced market note
example.text: Before Gefersa's meeting, Mekdes prepared a one-page note: recent indicative rate trend, the MPC No. 7 policy decision and inflation figures, the export surrender cut, and the drivers that could strengthen or weaken the birr. It gave no single forecast and ended with two scenarios and a sentence stating that the bank does not guarantee any rate. Hirut used it in her board paper.

scenario.title: A client wants a number
scenario.situation: Samuel, Gefersa's CEO, says: 'Just tell me where the rate will be in six months, and I will decide whether to hedge.'
scenario.question: What is the best response?
options: Give a precise forecast to win the deal
Say 'the birr will definitely weaken, so hedge everything'
Refuse to discuss rates at all
Explain the drivers and a range of scenarios from public sources, show the forward as the no-view price, and tie the decision to the hedging policy
scenario.explain: Balanced information is good advice and good conduct. A precise forecast is unreliable and, if wrong, invites a mis-selling complaint.

takeaways: A hedging policy covers objective, exposures, instruments, ratios and tenors, authority and reporting.
Hedge committed exposures at high ratios and forecast exposures at lower, layered ratios.
Show cost and protection across several rate scenarios, including one where the birr strengthens.
IFRS 9 hedge accounting needs documentation at inception to avoid profit swings.
Use the MPC release, indicative rate trend and IMF reviews to explain ranges, never promises.

quiz.q: A company hedges USD 2.4 million of a USD 3.0 million exposure. Hedge ratio?
Which exposure normally deserves the highest hedge ratio?
options: Committed payables due in three months
quiz.explain: Committed near-term flows are certain enough to hedge heavily.

quiz.q: USD 1 million is 60% hedged at 159.59 and the rest is bought at 180.00. Total birr cost?
Under IFRS 9, a forward hedging a forecast purchase is usually designated as a:
quiz.explain: Forecast transactions are hedged with cash flow hedges.

quiz.q: Ethiopian inflation 13.4% and US inflation 3.0%. The implied annual depreciation from the inflation gap is about:
Per MPC No. 7, the National Bank Rate was raised to:
quiz.explain: The Board raised the rate by 1 point to 16%.

modules.title: Bank-side risk and the capstone hedging proposal
modules.summary: Control the credit, market and conduct risks the bank takes when it sells FX products, then present a complete hedging proposal for the running case.
objectives: Set a counterparty credit limit for forwards using replacement cost and an add-on
Measure the bank's net open position against the SBB/96/2025 limit and cover client deals
Apply suitability checks and AML/CFT controls to FX products
Prepare and defend a client hedging proposal for the capstone

lessons.title: Counterparty credit limits for forwards
body: When a bank sells a client USD forward, it is exposed if the client fails before settlement and the rate has moved against the bank. The exposure has two parts: the current replacement cost (today's mark-to-market, if positive for the bank) and a potential future exposure add-on for how far the rate could move over the remaining tenor.

Credit approves a forward line as part of the client's facilities, using the bank's own method. The add-on should reflect the volatility of the birr since the float and the tenor of the contract. A typical teaching add-on for a six-month USD/ETB forward is 15% of notional; your bank's credit policy sets the real figure.

worked.title: Gefersa forward line (bank's teaching method, illustrative)

rows.label: Potential future exposure add-on, 15% of notional
Current replacement cost at trade date
Credit equivalent exposure at trade date
If the forward rate later falls to 150.00 (bank loses if Gefersa defaults)
Credit equivalent then: 30.9 + 77.1 (add-on kept for simplicity)

worked.note: Approve a forward line of about Birr 110 million credit equivalent within Gefersa's total facilities, and monitor it as rates move. If the birr strengthens, the client owes the bank more in value terms.

scenario.title: Which way does the risk run?
scenario.situation: Bank A sold Gefersa USD 3.22 million forward at 159.59. Three months later the birr has strengthened and the forward rate for the same date is 150.00.
scenario.question: Who is exposed to whom if Gefersa defaults now?
options: Gefersa to the bank, because Gefersa locked a worse rate
No one, forwards have no credit risk
The bank to Gefersa: the bank would have to replace a contract worth 159.59 with one at 150.00 and lose about Birr 30.9 million
scenario.explain: The contract is in the bank's favour, so a client default costs the bank the replacement loss of (159.59 minus 150.00) x 3.22 million. Clients that are out of the money on hedges are a credit risk to watch.

lessons.title: The bank's net open position
body: Every client deal changes the bank's FX position. Selling USD forward to an importer makes the bank short USD until it buys the same amount from an exporter, another bank or its own inflows. The overall open position is capped by the NBE.

Treasury manages the position, but sales staff must book deals immediately and tell treasury about large tickets before quoting firm rates. A large forward that pushes the bank beyond its limit at the close of the day becomes a regulatory breach.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/96/2025, Foreign Exchange Exposure Limits of Banks (in force 10 November 2025)
regulation.text: A bank's overall open foreign currency position may not exceed plus or minus 18% of its Tier 1 capital at the close of each business day. Banks set their own single-currency limits within that cap, must square any excess by the next business day and report daily. Breaches and late or false reporting carry fines. It repealed Directive No. SBB/27/2001.

worked.title: Bank A: position check after the Gefersa forward (illustrative)

rows.label: Gefersa forward sale: USD 3.22 million x 150.00 spot

worked.note: The deal fits comfortably. Treasury may still cover it with a forward purchase from an exporter to keep the book close to flat.

items.label: Exporter sells USD forward or spot

lessons.title: Suitability and mis-selling risk
body: A forward is a simple product but a binding one. A client who does not understand close-out, or who hedges more than its real exposure, can suffer a loss it did not expect and blame the bank. Mis-selling risk is a conduct risk and a reputational risk.

Before dealing, confirm the client has a real underlying exposure, that the amount and tenor match it, that the decision-maker understands the obligations, and that the client's board or policy authorises it. Never sell a hedge larger than the exposure, and never present a forward as a way to profit from rates.

regulation.source: National Bank of Ethiopia Proclamation No. 1359/2025, consumer protection (Art. 41)
regulation.text: The Proclamation gives the NBE a consumer protection mandate over financial services. For FX products this means fair treatment, clear disclosure of rates, fees and obligations, and handling complaints properly. The NBE's financial consumer protection directive (reported as FCP/01/2020) sets detailed rules; check the current text with compliance.

items.label: Exposure
items.text: Is there a documented underlying transaction?

items.label: Match
items.text: Amount and tenor no larger than the exposure

items.label: Understanding
items.text: Close-out, extension and cost explained and acknowledged

items.label: Authority
items.text: Board resolution or policy names who may deal

items.label: Record
items.text: Advice note and term sheet kept on file

example.title: A forward nobody explained
example.text: Gondar Building Materials PLC bought USD 600,000 forward to import steel, then its order was cancelled. Its owner, Alemayehu Desta, was surprised to be asked to pay a close-out loss and complained that no one had told him the contract was binding. The bank's file held a signed confirmation but no advice note or term sheet showing the risks had been explained. The bank settled the complaint and added a signed risk acknowledgement to every first forward.

scenario.title: A bigger hedge
scenario.situation: A trader asks Bank A for a USD 2 million 180-day forward. Its documented imports for the period are USD 800,000. The owner says he expects the birr to weaken and wants to 'make some money on the rest'.
scenario.question: What should the FX sales officer do?
options: Deal the full USD 2 million; the client is an adult
Offer a forward up to the USD 800,000 documented exposure and decline the speculative balance
Deal USD 2 million but charge a higher spread
Ask the client to split the deal across two banks
scenario.explain: A hedge should match a real exposure. The excess is speculation, which raises credit, conduct and compliance risk for the bank.

lessons.title: AML/CFT and conduct in FX business
body: FX cash notes, diaspora transfers and trade payments are classic channels for money laundering and terrorist financing. Watch for structuring of cash purchases or sales to stay under thresholds, third-party payments, and trade-based laundering through over-invoiced imports or under-invoiced exports.

Ethiopia's AML/CFT law requires customer due diligence, record keeping and suspicious transaction reporting to the Financial Intelligence Service. FXD/04/2026 removed the USD 10,000 cash declaration requirement, but that does not remove the duty to know the customer and report suspicion. The gap between bank rates and any remaining parallel market also creates pressure to bend rules.

example.title: An invoice that did not fit
example.text: Kidist Assefa, a trade officer, noticed that an importer's proforma for surgical gloves priced each box at three times the price on two earlier invoices from other suppliers. The importer wanted a forward for the full amount. She escalated to compliance, which found the supplier was linked to the importer's owner. The bank declined the forward and filed a suspicious transaction report.

scenario.title: Repeated cash purchases
scenario.situation: A walk-in customer buys USD cash notes just below the bank's internal review threshold on five consecutive days, each time with a different stated travel purpose.
scenario.question: What is the right action?
options: Serve the customer, each transaction is below the threshold
Treat the pattern as possible structuring, apply enhanced due diligence and escalate for a suspicious transaction report if not explained
Ask the customer to use a different branch
scenario.explain: Structuring is a red flag. The duty is to look at the pattern, not individual tickets, and to report suspicion through the bank's AML process.

lessons.title: Capstone: Gefersa's hedging proposal
body: Teams now bring the course together. The proposal states the exposure, the policy, the recommended hedge, the price and its build-up, the outcomes across scenarios, the bank-side approvals and the conditions. It must be short enough for Gefersa's board to read in ten minutes.

The client proposal counts for 40% of the course grade, the test for 30%, a work assignment for 20% (an FX exposure review of one real client of your branch or unit, anonymised) and participation for 10%. The pass mark is 70%.

worked.title: Gefersa: summary of the recommended proposal

rows.label: Committed exposure, month 6
rows.value: USD 4.6 million (after USD 0.4 million FCY balance)

rows.label: Birr cost locked on hedged part
Worst case total at 180.00, versus unhedged
Bank approvals
rows.value: Forward line about Birr 110 million credit equivalent; NOP headroom confirmed

rows.label: Forecast orders, months 3 to 12
rows.value: Layered forwards at 30% to 50% as orders are confirmed

rows.label: Conditions
rows.value: Board-approved hedging policy, framework agreement, monthly exposure report

worked.note: The proposal protects the fixed-price tender margin, keeps some flexibility, and fits the bank's limits.

items.label: Exposure
items.text: Map and net by currency and date

items.label: Policy
items.text: Objective, ratio, instruments, authority

items.label: Price
items.text: Forward from parity plus spread and credit charge

items.label: Scenarios
items.text: Outcomes at three or more rates

items.label: Bank side
items.text: Credit line, NOP, suitability, AML

items.label: Recommend
items.text: One clear proposal with conditions

scenario.title: A committee challenge
scenario.situation: At the presentation, a board member asks: 'If the birr strengthens to 150, we will have paid Birr 31 million more than we needed. Why should we accept that?'
scenario.question: Which answer best defends the proposal?
options: That Birr 31 million is the price of capping the worst case at Birr 762 million instead of Birr 828 million and of protecting the fixed-price tender margin, as the policy requires
The bank will refund the difference
You can cancel the forward for free if that happens
scenario.explain: The proposal is judged against the policy and the range of outcomes, not hindsight. The other answers are false or promise what the bank cannot deliver.

takeaways: Forward credit exposure = replacement cost + potential future exposure add-on; it changes as rates move.
SBB/96/2025 caps the overall open position at plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 capital at each day's close.
Book client deals immediately and warn treasury of large tickets before quoting firm.
Hedge only real, documented exposures, and explain close-out before the first deal.
A good proposal links exposure, policy, price, scenarios and bank-side approvals in one short paper.

quiz.q: A bank's Tier 1 capital is Birr 8,000 million. Its overall open position limit under SBB/96/2025 is:
quiz.explain: 18% x 8,000 = Birr 1,440 million either side.

quiz.q: If the limit is exceeded at the close of a day, the bank must:
options: Square the excess by the next business day
quiz.explain: The directive requires squaring by the next business day.

quiz.q: Notional Birr 300 million, add-on 15%, replacement cost Birr 10 million. Credit equivalent?
quiz.explain: 10 + 0.15 x 300 = Birr 55 million.

quiz.q: Selling USD forward to an importer leaves the bank:
quiz.explain: The bank owes USD in future and is short until it buys cover.

quiz.q: A client wants a forward three times its documented exposure. The main concern is:
quiz.explain: Hedges should match real exposures; the excess is speculation.

quiz.q: In the capstone grading, the client proposal counts for:
quiz.explain: Proposal 40%, test 30%, work assignment 20%, participation 10%.

exam.q: A client owes USD 2.5 million in 120 days and holds USD 0.5 million in its FCY account and expects USD 0.3 million of firm USD receipts into the same FCY account before then. Net committed exposure?
exam.explain: 2.5 minus 0.5 minus 0.3 = USD 1.7 million; only the net amount needs buying or hedging.

exam.q: A company booked a USD 1.5 million liability at Birr 57 and restates it at Birr 125. Its equity was Birr 200 million. Equity after the translation loss (ignoring tax) is about:
exam.explain: Loss = 1.5 million x 68 = Birr 102 million; 200 minus 102 = Birr 98 million.

exam.q: Which client most needs a financial hedge rather than a natural one?
options: An exporter paying USD costs from its retention account
A company with matching USD inflows and outflows each month
An importer with no FX income and fixed birr selling prices
exam.explain: It has no internal offset and cannot pass costs on.

exam.q: Spot 150.00, birr rate 16%, USD rate 4%, 180 days (days/360). Forward mid?
Using the same inputs, the 180-day forward points are:
A client says a forward at 159.59 'proves the bank expects 159.59'. The best correction is:
options: Forwards are set by the NBE
Forwards are always above future spot
Forwards come from the interest gap, not a forecast
Forwards are the indicative rate plus a fee
exam.explain: Interest rate parity sets the forward; future spot may differ.

exam.q: Forward mid 154.08, spread 1.10, credit charge 0.50, notional USD 2 million. Birr cost locked?
exam.explain: Rate 155.68 x 2 million = Birr 311.36 million.

exam.q: A client cancels USD 500,000 of a forward at 158.09 when the market forward is 152.00. The client:
exam.explain: (158.09 minus 152.00) x 500,000 = Birr 3.045 million owed by the client.

exam.q: Which statement about FX swaps is correct?
options: They create an open position for both sides
They need a long-term yield curve
They combine a spot exchange with a reverse forward, and their price is the forward points
They are the same as options
exam.explain: A swap moves liquidity, not risk; its price is the points.

exam.q: A USD call has strike 158 and premium 5. At expiry the rate is 154. Effective cost per USD is:
exam.explain: Lapse, buy at 154, plus premium 5 = 159.

exam.q: Which product is explicitly allowed for customers in the directives reviewed for this course?
exam.explain: FXD/04/2026 allows banks to offer forward rates.

exam.q: Under FXD/04/2026, approval of external loans and supplier credits now rests with:
options: Banks, with monthly reporting to the NBE
exam.explain: Banks approve without prior NBE approval and report monthly.

exam.q: A hotel has 70% birr revenue and 100% USD debt service. A 20% depreciation most directly:
options: Raises birr debt service and lowers DSCR
Only changes translation of fixed assets
exam.explain: USD debt service costs more birr while most revenue does not rise.

exam.q: Exposure USD 4 million; 75% hedged at 160; the rest bought at 175. Total birr cost?
exam.explain: 3 million x 160 + 1 million x 175 = 480 + 175 = Birr 655 million.

exam.q: A forecast purchase hedged with a forward, without hedge accounting, will most likely cause:
options: Profit volatility from fair value changes before the purchase is recognised
exam.explain: The derivative is marked to market through profit or loss.

exam.q: Ethiopian inflation 13.4%, US inflation 2.5%. The inflation-gap guide implies annual depreciation of about:
Bank A has Tier 1 of Birr 10,000 million and an open position of minus Birr 1,500 million. It sells a client USD 2 million forward at spot 150. The new position and status:
options: Minus Birr 1,800 million, within the Birr 1,800 million limit, with no headroom left
exam.explain: Limit 18% x 10,000 = 1,800. Selling USD adds minus 300, giving minus 1,800: at the limit.

exam.q: A forward is in the bank's favour by Birr 20 million and the add-on is Birr 40 million. Credit equivalent exposure is:
exam.explain: Replacement cost 20 + add-on 40 = Birr 60 million.

exam.q: A trader requests a forward double its documented imports to profit from depreciation. The best response is:
options: Deal the full amount at a higher spread
Refer the client to an offshore bank
Limit the hedge to the documented exposure and record the advice
exam.explain: Hedges match real exposures; speculation raises conduct and credit risk.

exam.q: A walk-in customer buys USD cash just under the review threshold every day for a week. The correct step is:
options: Apply enhanced due diligence to the pattern and escalate for possible suspicious transaction reporting
